data.title: AudioCodes Adopts Rule 10b5-1 Share Repurchase Plan to Enable Structured Buybacks
data.description:
The latest update is out from Audiocodes ( (AUDC) ).

On September 14, 2026, AudioCodes Ltd. announced that it had adopted and approved a stock trading plan under Rule 10b5-1 of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to facilitate repurchases of its ordinary shares. The plan is designed to allow the company to buy back stock even during periods when it might otherwise be restricted by insider trading laws or self-imposed trading blackout windows.

Under the newly approved Rule 10b5-1 plan, an independent broker will execute share repurchases on AudioCodes’ behalf within predefined pricing parameters and subject to market volume and timing limits set by Rule 10b-18. The move signals a structured approach to capital return and may improve flexibility in executing buybacks, potentially supporting share liquidity and providing an additional tool for managing the company’s capital structure.

data.description:

Amundi has launched a new employee share ownership plan, We Share Amundi, a capital increase reserved for staff, early retirees and retirees across multiple countries, offering a 30% discount to the market-based subscription price of €66.63 per share. The scheme is designed to strengthen employees’ participation in the group’s growth and economic value creation, with a five-year lock-up period and access via dedicated employee mutual funds or direct share subscriptions.

The offer runs from 14 to 25 September 2026, with a maximum of 1,000,000 new shares to be issued, representing less than 0.5% of Amundi’s share capital and voting rights, implying a negligible impact on earnings per share. Employees, who currently hold 2.22% of the company’s capital, face an individual subscription cap of €40,000, and allocation mechanisms will scale back larger orders if demand exceeds the envelope, reinforcing Amundi’s strategy of broad-based employee ownership without materially diluting existing shareholders.
